config.title: Leipziger Platz Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: The octagon, the Wall, Wertheim and what to see today.

items.q: What is Leipziger Platz in Berlin?
items.a: It is the **octagonal square** directly east of Potsdamer Platz, laid out between **1731 and 1734** as part of the Friedrichstadt and named after the Battle of Leipzig in **1814**. Leipziger Straße runs east from it.

items.q: Why is Leipziger Platz an octagon?
items.a: It was planned that way in the 1730s, inside the Potsdam Gate of the old customs wall, and its first name was the **Octogon**. When the square was rebuilt after 1990, the city kept the eight-sided outline and made every new building follow it.

items.q: Did the Berlin Wall run through Leipziger Platz?
items.a: Yes. From **August 1961** the square lay in the death strip, and the inner wall facing East Berlin ran **diagonally across the octagon** towards the Brandenburg Gate. A few slabs of it still stand on the north and south sides.

items.q: What stood on the site of the Mall of Berlin?
items.a: The **Wertheim** department store by Alfred Messel, opened in **1897** and one of the largest in Europe. It was taken from the Jewish Wertheim family in **1938**, bombed in 1944 and cleared in the 1950s. The Tresor club used its vaults from 1991 to 2005.

items.q: How long do you need at Leipziger Platz?
items.a: **15 minutes** is enough for the octagon, the Wall pieces and the Wertheim site. With **30 to 45 minutes** you can add the old gate opening, the Canadian Embassy corner and the Bundesrat building on Leipziger Straße.

items.q: Is the Mall of Berlin open on Sundays?
items.a: Mostly not. It is open **Monday to Saturday, 10:00 to 20:00**, and opens on only a few Sundays a year, in 2026 on **6 and 20 December**. The square itself is open at all times.
